Text: "MP3

Technicolor (formerly called Thomson Consumer Electronics) claims to control MP3 licensing of the Layer 3 patents in many countries, including the United States, Japan, Canada and EU countries. Technicolor has been actively enforcing these patents."

We need to identify entities: MP3 (maybe a concept), Technicolor (company), Thomson Consumer Electronics (former name), Layer 3 patents (maybe a concept), many countries (list). The claim: "Technicolor claims to control MP3 licensing of the Layer 3 patents in many countries, including the United States, Japan, Canada and EU countries."

So we can produce a triplet: (Technicolor, claim, control of MP3 licensing of Layer 3 patents) but need to break down.

Better: relation "claims" maybe "claim" predicate. Object: "control MP3 licensing of the Layer 3 patents". Could separate: (Technicolor, claims to control, MP3 licensing of Layer 3 patents). But we need relation names like "claims" maybe "claim". Use "claim" as relation.

Also we have "formerly called" relation: (Technicolor, former name, Thomson Consumer Electronics). Actually "Technicolor (formerly called Thomson Consumer Electronics)" indicates that Technicolor was formerly called Thomson Consumer Electronics. So relation: "former name" or "named after"? Use "former name". So (Technicolor, former name, Thomson Consumer Electronics).

Third: "Technicolor has been actively enforcing these patents." So (Technicolor, enforcement activity, Layer 3 patents) maybe relation "enforces". So (Technicolor, enforces, Layer 3 patents). Also "actively" is modality? It's an adverb indicating manner, not modality. Could be qualifier "manner" but not required. Could add qualifier "activity" but not needed.

Also "in many countries, including the United States, Japan, Canada and EU countries." This qualifies the claim of control. So we attach qualifiers to the claim triplet: relation "applies in" or "location". Use "location" qualifier. For each country? Could list as separate qualifiers? Possibly one qualifier with object "United States, Japan, Canada, EU countries". Could be separate qualifiers each. Simpler: one qualifier with relation "location" and object "United States, Japan, Canada, EU countries". Or "countries". We'll use "location" qualifier.

Also "MP3 licensing" is object concept. So maybe object: "MP3 licensing of Layer 3 patents". Could split: (Technicolor, claims to control, MP3 licensing) with qualifier "of patents" but maybe too complex. We'll keep object as "MP3 licensing of Layer 3 patents". object_type: "licensing" maybe "intellectual property licensing". We'll set object_type "licensing".

Now define subject_type: Technicolor is a "company". object_type: for former name: "company". For claim: object_type "licensing". For enforcement: object_type "patent". For "Layer 3 patents": object_type "patent". For "MP3": object_type "format". But MP3 appears as concept but not as subject.

We also might have a triplet: (MP3, category, audio format) but not in text. Not needed.
